body.x: CREAM Corp. (CEO Kim Jisung) has announced its participation in CES 2025 from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas at the K-Startup Pavilion. Founded with the vision of enabling anyone to turn their imagination into content anytime, anywhere, CREAM has been developing its proprietary technology as a personalized AI assistant for creators.

AiD simplifies the content creation, especially in webtoon production, by automating intensive tasks. This allows creators to dedicate more time and resources to the artistic aspects of their work, ultimately improving quality, consistency, and efficiency. Through this platform, CREAM has distinguished itself domestically and aims to expand its presence globally by introducing its technology at CES 2025.

The AiD platform focuses on learning common artistic styles and techniques from as few as five uploaded images. Leveraging “Micro AI Tuning” technology, it analyzes intricate character details, such as facial features, clothing, line art, and coloring styles, to produce consistent and high-quality outputs. After approximately one hour of training, users can generate diverse images in the same style, receiving results praised for their precision and reliability by a growing local and international user base.

AiD further enhances usability by providing outputs in a format with separated layers. This enables users to make edits effortlessly or integrate the images directly into their projects. This feature has been especially well-received for its practicality and flexibility.

“AiD is an innovative tool that empowers creators to produce richer and higher-quality content,” a company representative explained. “It stands out from similar commercial services with its superior accuracy and functionality. Users have consistently reported significant time and cost savings.” The representative added, “As the global webtoon market grows, we aim to leverage our domestic success to expand into the U.S. and Japanese markets, recognized as hubs for comics and manga. At CES 2025, we look forward to connecting with industry leaders from various countries and achieving meaningful results.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
